name: Neue Rechte
summary: The German Neue Rechte is a loose network of right-wing intellectuals around the Institut fur Staatspolitik, the journal Sezession and the Antaios publishing house, who draw on the Conservative Revolution of the Weimar Republic. They defend a homogeneous, volkisch idea of the people and nation against pluralist democracy, individual human rights and mass immigration, and pursue a metapolitical fight for cultural hegemony. They distance themselves from National Socialism and say they respect all cultures in their own homelands (ethnopluralism).
scope: The German Neue Rechte in the narrow sense of Pfahl-Traughber: the intellectual network around Kubitschek, Weissmann, the IfS and Sezession, 2000s to 2020s, with its Conservative Revolution references (Schmitt, Junger, Moeller van den Bruck). It excludes the French Nouvelle Droite (its own entry), the AfD, Pegida, the Junge Freiheit as a whole, and the street Identitarian movement. Positions come from the scholarship and from attributed primary passages reproduced by Huber; economics, religion and party strategy are documented splits or left unspecified.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Pfahl-Traughber names an ethnically and politically homogeneous people and a volkisch nationalism as basic positions, and Sezession authors state that a people needs at least a minimum of homogeneity (Waldstein, Paulwitz).

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ethnopluralism, as Pfahl-Traughber and Meyer describe it, aims at preserving each people's identity in its ancestral space, and the IfS and Sezession treat national identity as the thing under threat.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Pfahl-Traughber states that the Neue Rechte wants collective rights for peoples in place of individual human rights, and Sander (Sezession 92) argues that making the individual absolute atomises the community.

person-over-state.rationale: The stated preference for collective over individual rights and for duty and service to the state (Huber ch. 20) conflicts with treating no person as a mere means to community ends.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Huber reports that Sezession authors stress duty and service to the state and the collective over individual needs, though Kubitschek ends the duty to serve a state judged unworthy.

natural-rulers.rationale: Pfahl-Traughber lists elite ideas set against the ideal of equality as a basic position, and Huber reports that the authors endorse the elite idea with authority and leadership (Wessels calls it a pillar of right-wing outlook).

strong-leader.rationale: Huber reports that the authors endorse the elite idea together with authority and leadership, and Kubitschek laments the unled mass; no concrete system is specified (Pfahl-Traughber).

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Pfahl-Traughber: the identitarian conception of democracy assumes a unity of rulers and ruled that excludes opposition and pluralism; Huber reports Lehnert calling communities of conviction undemocratic.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Neue Rechte counters the pluralist, competitive-election conception of democracy with a homogeneous one resting on the unity of the people, as Pfahl-Traughber explains with Schmitt.

democracy-best.rationale: Pfahl-Traughber notes that they profess democracy but redefine it, while aiming at a spiritual overcoming of the democratic constitutional state, so the record points both ways.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Sezession authors campaign against mass immigration (Menzel, Weissmann, Kubitschek, Meyer as quoted by Huber), and the ethnopluralist programme Pfahl-Traughber describes goes further, to return.

open-borders.rationale: Authors in Sezession treat immigration as a threat to the German and European people's identity (Huber ch. 20, Menzel, Ley), so eventually open borders is the opposite of their position.

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: Pfahl-Traughber says ethnopluralism holds that identity is best kept in the home countries, which makes return necessary; he does not say all authors specify the mechanism or include citizens.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Authors hold that community requires at least minimal homogeneity of the people (Waldstein: "jede Gemeinschaftsausrichtung setzt ein Minimum an Homogenitat im Volk voraus") and denounce a multicultural experiment.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Paulwitz laments that citizenship and ethnic belonging no longer coincide, and Sommerfeld distinguishes descent Germans from passport Germans (Sezession 46, 88, as reported by Huber).

elite-replacement.rationale: Later Sezession authors (Wiesberg, Scholdt, Meyer) say governments and elites pursue population replacement, but Weissmann (2012) denies a master plan, so the milieu is split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Ethnopluralism officially denies a ranking of cultures and gives all peoples equal worth (Pfahl-Traughber), though some authors call the Germans a specially distinguished people (Huber).

universal-morality.rationale: The Neue Rechte rests on anti-universalism and rejects the Enlightenment and universal equality ideology (Hagedorny, Meyer, Pfahl-Traughber).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Pfahl-Traughber says elite ideas are proclaimed against the equality ideal and the Conservative Revolution was opposed to equal worth, yet ethnopluralism claims equal worth of peoples.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The Neue Rechte proclaims elite ideas against the ideal of equality (Pfahl-Traughber).

nation-first.rationale: Meyer reports that the state and its interests hold primacy in Neue Rechte foreign policy thinking, and Pfahl-Traughber that volkisch nationalism replaces the primacy of human rights.

national-self-determination.rationale: Huber reports a Sezession author calling life in one's own nation and state a right whose denial is despotic, and that sovereignty is central to the authors.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Huber reports that authors see sovereignty threatened by the European Union (Dirsch, Kaiser calls it an elite project); the milieu agrees on loss of identity more than on remedy.

multipolar-world.rationale: Meyer reports a milieu preference for a plural world in which the USA is one voice among many (Straub), and Europe independent of American hegemony.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Meyer: for large parts of the Neue Rechte, Germany is predestined for a third way between capitalism and communism, and Bolshevism is seen as liberalism radicalised.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pfahl-Traughber lists market economy versus welfare state among the questions on which the network differs.

cut-welfare.rationale: Pfahl-Traughber lists more market economy or more welfare state as a question on which the network is divided.

traditional-family.rationale: Kaiser (Sezession 98) calls family, people and homeland the unshakeable pillars of an organic order, and Sander makes the same point (reported by Huber).

restore-past-order.rationale: Pfahl-Traughber: the Conservative Revolution referred to supposedly lost values to be revived (elite, leadership, God, nation, order), and the Neue Rechte transfers them to the present.

national-rebirth.rationale: Huber reports a repeated diagnosis of national decline and decadence with renewal of national identity as the remedy (Susswold, Sander, Kubitschek).

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: Huber: the authors reject critical reckoning with the Nazi past as national weakness, calling it a guilt cult and a monumentalisation of guilt.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Kaiser (Sezession 84) restates Gramsci that cultural hegemony precedes political power and sees the Federal Republic under a left-liberal hegemony; Pfahl-Traughber confirms the Gramscian strategy.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Hagedorny documents that the IfS and Weissmann reject the Islamophobic line, while others in the milieu are hostile, so the milieu divides on this.

reification.rationale: Kaiser (Solidarischer Patriotismus, 2020) states that capitalism and its inherent logic objectify human relations, as Pfahl-Traughber reports.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Sommerfeld warns that global uniformity of consumption pushes the own culture on the defensive, and Kaiser attacks the capitalist logic (Ebert, Pfahl-Traughber in Randgange).

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Huber reports that Sezession authors criticise the modernisation of the Christian churches and prize traditional, sacral religion (Lichtmesz, Lehnert, Kositza).

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Kaiser's Solidarischer Patriotismus, the one book from the milieu on social policy, joins patriotism with a social question from the right (Pfahl-Traughber); the milieu also has a market-liberal wing.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Meyer reports Straub and Mohler holding that NATO lost its sense with the Cold War and that Europe must free itself from American tutelage.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Huber reports early Sezession expecting assimilation as the answer to immigration problems, and the IfS brochure (Hagedorny) finds limited assimilation of Muslims conceivable, while ethnopluralism (Pfahl-Traughber) holds that identity is kept by return.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Huber quotes Scholdt in Sezession mocking the swap of fascism for antifascism and a thought police of militant democracy, and Kaiser attacks a front of capital and antifascism.
